context.title: Coups and the House of Omri
context.summary: Israel goes through a string of assassinations and short reigns until Omri takes power and builds a new capital at Samaria. His son Ahab marries Jezebel and promotes Baal worship.
context.background: The Bible gives Omri only a few verses, but outside sources show he was a major figure: Assyrian records later called Israel 'the house of Omri,' and the Moabite Stone recalls his rule over Moab. Jezebel was a princess of Sidon, a Phoenician city devoted to Baal.

customs.note: A Canaanite storm god believed to send rain and fertility. This sets up the drought that begins in the next chapter.

watchFor: Each new king does 'worse than all that were before him' (vv. 25, 30).
Hiel's rebuilding of Jericho fulfills Joshua's ancient curse (v. 34).

w: and you have caused to sin

people.name: Baasha
people.summary: Bravery, the third king of the separate kingdom of Israel, and founder of its second dynasty (1 Kings 15; 16; 2 Chr. 16:1-6). He was the son of Ahijah of the tribe of Issachar.

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

people.name: Jeroboam
people.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

people.name: Elah
people.summary: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Asa
people.summary: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14).

people.name: Zimri
people.summary: Murdered Elah at Tirzah, and succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He reigned only seven days, for Omri, whom the army elected as king, laid siege to Tirzah, whereupon Zimri set fire to the palace and perished amid its ruins (11-20).

people.name: Omri
people.summary: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-27), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927).

people.name: Tibni
people.summary: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch.

people.name: Ahab
people.summary: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel, who exercised a very evil influence over him.

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

people.name: Jezebel
people.summary: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind.

people.name: Ethbaal
people.summary: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

people.name: Abiram
people.summary: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16:34), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

people.name: Hiel
people.summary: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites.

people.name: Segub
people.summary: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite.

places.name: Tirzah
places.summary: An old royal city of the Canaanites, which was destroyed by Joshua (Josh. 12:24). Jeroboam chose it for his residence, and he removed to it from Shechem, which at first he made the capital of his kingdom.

places.name: Gibbethon
places.summary: A height, a city of the Philistines in the territory of Dan, given to the Kohathites (Josh. 19:44; 21:23). Nadab the king of Israel, while besieging it, was slain under its walls by Baasha, one of his own officers (1 Kings 15:27).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

events.title: Reign of Baasha
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 15:33–16:5. People: Baasha. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 24 years.

events.title: Reign of Elah
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:6–8. People: Elah. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 2 years.

events.title: Reign of Zimri
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:15–16. People: Zimri. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 7 days.

events.title: Reign of Tibni
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:21–22. People: Tibni. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 4 years.

events.title: Reign of Omri
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:22–28. People: Omri. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 12 years.

events.title: Death of Omri
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:28. People: Omri. Place: Samaria.

events.title: Reign of Ahab
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 16:28–30. People: Ahab. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 22 years.
